# Gap-free acquisition by bounded nonlinear projection and corrected outputs

Root constructive draft, 2026-11-01. Pending independent receiving. Built during parallel work with the scalar constructor. This replaces the proposed inverse-Gram linear realization, not the physical source contract. Governing N1515 already supplied noisy bounded-l1 projection, kernel Frank-Wolfe, and failed-successor retention. The proposed distinction is expanded m*aconv(V), nonlinear task-by-task projection, corrected scalar outputs and rank-log acquisition, rather than a globally invariant unit hull or linear intertwiner. Projection, Frank-Wolfe, dual-weighted correction, and determinant potentials are prior mathematical machinery. Novelty and consequential application remain unresolved.

## Source and task

Real Hilbert contractions T_a, ||f||<=1, finite alphabet closed under supplied actual adjoints, fresh bounded binary scalar reports of Gamma(u,v)=<T_u f,T_v f>. Conditional unbiasedness, stationary preparation where used, controls, episodes and bit costs remain charged. Requested output is F(w)=<f,T_w f> for |w|<=H. No general readout, state, conditional record law or planner is supplied.

Dictionary V consists only of actual descriptors, including f. At size m, put B=m and K_m={Vc: ||c||_1<=B}. This is a symmetric convex subset of the physical Hilbert space, not an assumed coordinate representation. It need not approximate every reachable state before future tasks arrive. No physical superposition preparation is required: combinations are mathematical calculations of measured scalar means.

Set lambda=epsilon/(128 H^4). At precision epoch b=nextpower2(m), acquire/cache all needed G=V*V, K_a=V*T_a V, H_a=(T_a V)*(T_a V) entries to absolute accuracy

 alpha=lambda/[128(b+4)b²].

All statements below are on their simultaneous confidence event. Use the same accuracy for prefix self/cross returns. Finite family/confidence allocation and permanent failure latch follow the earlier scalar receiver, but its inverse-Gram model is not reused.

# Independent rounded-FW finite-bit addendum — 2026-11-01

This independently audits the root's subsequent rounded-step proposal. I read and verified the actual author file ROUNDED_PROJECTION_SOLVER.md SHA256 972ee67b866093f791d11e8081d379bbdf27037f80549b92c8d29d690ca3640b, together with current main construction SHA256 4dd9265425b1ef0f78c487602c63e6cd8d78b429c1cf7bc67155981e8ad1632f; the acceptance below binds those bytes. It supplements, rather than retroactively changes, the original unrounded proof recorded in RECEIPT.md (original historical SHA256 c298209577337f2aae8fba8c1f16d55e8641c003ca67bf880c68962d32b8bae9; subsequently given a current-byte/update notice). That receipt's larger digital accuracy cost concerned its explicitly UNROUNDED solver. The rounded solver below has a different and better certified bit-work bound.

## Judgment

The rounded solver is sound. It preserves the exact gap stopping criterion and therefore all statistical projection, corrected-output, witness and lifetime proofs in the preceding receipt. It gives a sufficient full DIGITAL accuracy factor lambda^-2 up to logarithms, not merely the source-shot factor, while retaining large polynomial rank/horizon dependence. No implementation speedup, optimality, or novelty follows.

## Descent proof independent of coefficient conditioning

At size m, B=m, C=16mB^2, delta=B^2 alpha. Let the exact empirical gradient be g=2Gbar c-2Khat d and let s be the exact l1-ball minimizing vertex. When gap=<g,c-s> exceeds delta, form

    c'=(1-theta)c+theta s,  theta=delta/C.

Then round each coordinate TOWARD ZERO to a fixed dyadic grid h=2^-p satisfying

    h <= delta^2/(24CBm).

Both c' and its rounded version c'' remain in the l1 ball. The entire segment joining them lies in that convex ball. Binary sample means imply |Khat_ij|<=1. Also |Gbar_ij|<=2: off-diagonal entries are empirical means, and the diagonal shift m alpha<1. Thus on the whole ball

    ||gradient qbar||_infty <=2(2B)+2B=6B.

The rounding displacement has l1 norm at most mh, so integration of the gradient along that feasible segment yields

    qbar(c'')-qbar(c') <=6Bmh <=delta^2/(4C).

Curvature gives qbar(c')-qbar(c)<=-theta gap+(C/2)theta^2 < -delta^2/(2C). Therefore each nonterminal rounded step decreases the SAME exact empirical objective by at least delta^2/(4C). This is not an assumption that rounding preserves the FW gap
